definitions.explanation: Physical bending or winding of a road, river, or path.
Figuratively, the various difficulties, changes, and complications encountered along the way. Very commonly used in the expression 紆余曲折.

examples.japanese: {道|みち}が{曲折|きょくせつ}している。
{川|かわ}は{山間部|さんかんぶ}を{曲折|きょくせつ}しながら{流|なが}れている。
examples.english: The river flows through the mountainous area, winding as it goes.

examples.japanese: {急|きゅう}な{曲折|きょくせつ}が{続|つづ}く{山道|やまみち}は{運転|うんてん}が{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: Mountain roads with sharp bends in succession are difficult to drive.

examples.japanese: {紆余|うよ}{曲折|きょくせつ}を{経|へ}て{完成|かんせい}した。
examples.english: It was completed after many twists and turns.

examples.japanese: この{計画|けいかく}は{紆余|うよ}{曲折|きょくせつ}があったが、{最終的|さいしゅうてき}に{成功|せいこう}した。
examples.english: This plan had many complications, but it ultimately succeeded.

examples.japanese: {人生|じんせい}の{紆余|うよ}{曲折|きょくせつ}を{乗|の}り{越|こ}えて、{今|いま}の{自分|じぶん}がある。
examples.english: I am who I am today because I overcame life's many ups and downs.

notes:
USAGE:
The figurative sense (sense 2) is far more common than the literal sense. {曲折|きょくせつ} almost always appears in the four-character compound {紆余|うよ}{曲折|きょくせつ}, which is one of the most frequently used yojijukugo.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {紆余|うよ}{曲折|きょくせつ} (twists and turns, complications)
- {紆余|うよ}{曲折|きょくせつ}を{経|へ}て (after many twists and turns)
- {紆余|うよ}{曲折|きょくせつ}があった (there were complications)
- {曲折|きょくせつ}した{道|みち} (a winding road)
